Commercial licenses come first, because size or service decides them. Then come the everyday classes: D, the junior DJ, the hire-carrying E, and the motorcycle classes M and MJ. A current out-of-state or foreign license is honored. Nobody under sixteen may drive. New permanent residents must trade in their old license within thirty days. And holding licenses from two states at once is generally unlawful. The manual adds a warning about documents: forging or altering any motor-vehicle document is a crime. Carrying many people, running an Article nineteen-A bus, or hauling placarded hazmat is service. Ordinary cars and small trailers stay non-commercial. Class DJ is the junior version. It starts at sixteen, with lower weight and towing caps under junior limits. So a sixteen-year-old starts with DJ, while an eighteen-year-old, or a seventeen-year-old with driver education, can hold Class D. a New York photo card counts six.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"How many points must your name proofs add up to when you apply?","fact_ids":["sec01-F11"]},"answer":{"text":"Six points, with at least one signed document.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11"]},"rationale":{"text":"A current New York photo card alone is worth six points unless expired over two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Applying for a first license","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"The application path.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"The six-point identity system.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson walks through applying for your first license.
